title: Onboarding Data Sovereignty Verification and Localization Test Plan
author: Priya Nair
body:
Summary:
This test plan defines the verification and evidence requirements for customer onboarding where data sovereignty, localization, or regional residency are contractual or regulatory requirements. It covers Private and Dedicated deployment modes and maps concrete test steps, acceptance criteria, required artifacts, and escalation paths for failures.

Who this is for:
- Customer Success Engineering (CSE) and Solutions Engineering (SE) owners running the cutover/test window.
- Customer security/compliance contacts and their audit teams.
- DevOps/SRE and Private deployment engineers responsible for network and key management configuration.

Scope and constraints:
- Applies to enterprise customers requesting region-locked data storage, processing, or egress restrictions (examples: EU-only, UK-only, APAC-only).
- Includes control-plane (metadata), data-plane (payloads, logs, metrics) and third-party integrations that may export customer data.
- Excludes purely hosted multi-tenant (non-dedicated) customers unless explicitly contracted.

Acceptance criteria (must all be met for signoff):
1) Data residency: All customer PII and customer-configured data streams are persisted only to allowed region(s) as documented in the customer contract.
2) Network isolation: No unexpected public egress from the private tenant VPC; all egress destinations are approved.
3) KMS enforcement: Customer-managed keys (CMKs/KMS/HSM) are in use and cannot be bypassed by service operators.
4) Audit logs: Ingestion and storage of audit logs are retained at configured retention (min 365 days) and include the fields: timestamp, actor, operation, resource, region, request-id.
5) Telemetry leakage: No telemetry packets containing customer data fields (e.g., prompt text, outputs, embeddings) are forwarded out-of-region or to vendor endpoints.
6) Observability and alerting: A synthetic test and alert rule detect cross-region egress within 10 minutes of occurrence.

Ownership and roles:
- CSE owner: coordinates the test window and evidence collection. (Example: Priya Nair)
- Private-deployments engineer: runs in-environment verification and fixes (Example: Lena Park)
- Security reviewer: validates audit evidence and signs acceptance (Example: Diego Morales)
- Customer contact: provides approved egress and org-level allowlists.

Test matrix (high-level):
| Test area | Target system | Success indicator | Artifact |
|-----------|---------------|-------------------|----------|
| Data at rest residency | Object store / DB | All persisted objects have region label matching contract | sample object manifest (JSON) + storage ACLs |
| Data in transit locality | Ingress/Egress proxies | Packets do not traverse disallowed regions (no AS path to disallowed regions) | tcpdump pcap, traceroute outputs |
| KMS enforcement | KMS/HSM | Decrypt operations require CMK tied to customer project | KMS logs (key-id), policy snippet |
| Audit logging retention | Audit pipeline | Logs appear in customer-controlled store and preserved for 365d | sample logs, retention settings screenshot |
| Telemetry scrub & egress | Telemetry forwarder | No payload-level fields present in telemetry samples | sampled telemetry JSONs with redaction markers |

Pre-test checklist (run 24–72 hours before window):
- Confirm contract region(s) and document exact ISO region codes.
- Validate network ACLs and peering configs with customer net-team; collect approved CIDR lists.
- Provision or verify customer KMS keys and key policies.
- Ensure audit log export target (S3/GCS/Blob) is reachable from tenant and retention config set.
- Schedule test window and invite stakeholders.

Verification procedures (step-by-step):
1) Provisioning verification (performed by Private-deployments engineer)
   a) Confirm tenant placement: run infra query and record placement tags:
      - CLI: redwoodctl tenant describe --tenant <TENANT_ID> --fields placement,tags
      - Expected: placement.region == "eu-west-1" (or contracted code)
   b) Validate storage endpoints: curl to metadata endpoint to confirm storage URLs contain region identifier.
2) Data residency smoke test (run with test payloads)
   a) Ingest synthetic payloads labeled with unique test-id and region tag.
      - Example payload: { "test_id": "residency-2026-01-15-<uuid>", "pii": "redacted-for-test" }
   b) Query storage replication index to confirm object located in allowed bucket(s).
   c) Artifact: JSON manifest listing object key, storage path, storage-region.
3) KMS and key policy verification
   a) Attempt decrypt via an operator service account that is NOT authorized; expect failure.
   b) Show key policy document where service principal is scoped to customer role. Include KMS log extract showing decrypt attempt failures and successful decrypts from allowed roles.
4) Network path and egress validation
   a) From an in-tenant VM, run traceroute to an external endpoint and capture AS path. Confirm no hops into disallowed geographies.
   b) Capture full tcpdump during a synthetic request that touches model inference and telemetry. Save pcap as evidence.
5) Telemetry leakage and scrub check
   a) Trigger a model request that includes a short prompt with a known marker string.
   b) Check telemetry forwarder samples for presence of the marker in any field. Marker must not appear in telemetry sent to external endpoints. Provide sanitized telemetry samples and forwarder config showing redaction rules.
6) Audit log retention and content verification
   a) Pull last 72 hours of audit events for the tenant and search for the required fields.
   b) Provide sample log entries and retention policy config.

Automated checks (recommended):
- A synthetic job that performs the steps in (2) and (5) once per hour during the cutover period and reports failures to the CSE Slack channel and PagerDuty (if severity is high).
- A periodic compliance scan (weekly) that validates storage-region tags versus allowed region list and emits anomalies.

Evidence artifacts (required for signoff):
- JSON manifest of test objects (object-key, region, timestamp).
- PCAP and traceroute logs for the network validation step.
- KMS access logs showing key-id and caller identity.
- Telemetry samples (sanitized) and forwarder config file.
- Audit log extracts (min 72-hour window) and retention configuration screenshots.
- Signed acceptance email from customer compliance contact.

Failure modes and escalation matrix:
- If a cross-region object is discovered: Pause provisioning, notify SE and Security, open internal incident with severity P0 if > 100 objects or P1 otherwise. Immediate remediation: revoke write permissions, run data-delete and re-ingest in correct region.
- If KMS policy is mis-specified: Roll back key policy to deny-by-default, work with customer to re-apply policy. Escalate to security within 2 hours.
- If telemetry leakage is detected: Disable telemetry forwarder to external endpoints and preserve samples for triage. Escalate to telemetry-owner and legal if customer data present.

Signoff and artifacts delivery:
1) CSE compiles the evidence zip with filenames and index.json manifest.
2) Security reviewer confirms policy and signs the Security Acceptance form (template below).
3) Customer compliance contact acknowledges with signed email or signed PDF form.
4) Store artifacts under the secure evidence bucket with path: s3://evidence.redwood/onboarding/<TENANT_ID>/data-sovereignty/<DATE>/ and add retention tag "onboarding-evidence: true".

Evidence filename conventions (required):
- <TENANT_ID>_residency-manifest_<YYYYMMDD>.json
- <TENANT_ID>_pcap_network-validate_<YYYYMMDD>.pcap
- <TENANT_ID>_kms-log_<YYYYMMDD>.json
- <TENANT_ID>_telemetry-sample_<YYYYMMDD>.json
- <TENANT_ID>_audit-extract_<YYYYMMDD>.json

Sample Security Acceptance snippet (copy into signoff document):
"We, the Redwood Security Review team, confirm that based on the submitted artifacts for TENANT_ID <TENANT_ID> on <DATE>, the controls for data residency, KMS enforcement, audit logging, and telemetry redaction meet the contracted requirements. Signed: <Reviewer Name>."

Appendix A — Example redaction config (telemetry forwarder)
---yaml
forwarder:
  redact_fields:
    - prompt_text
    - response_text
    - embeddings_payload
  redact_strategy: hash
  external_endpoints: [] # must be empty unless explicitly approved
  validation_mode: sampling
---

Appendix B — Quick CLI snippets
- List tenant placement:
  redwoodctl tenant describe --tenant <TENANT_ID> --fields placement,tags
- Extract audit logs (example):
  aws s3 cp s3://customer-audit-bucket/tenants/<TENANT_ID>/audit/ ./ --recursive --profile customer-audit

Related references:
- Confluence: Data Residency Policy (security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention/policy-2025)
- Eng: Private Deployment Reference Architecture (eng-private-deployments/reference-architectures/private-vpc-patterns)

Notes and best practices:
- Run the telemetry leakage test with several marker patterns, not just one to reduce false negatives.
- Keep an immutable copy of evidence for 365 days in case of downstream audits.
- If the customer requires local only operator access restrictions, coordinate a separate Access Control Review; this test plan does not assert operator access model changes beyond KMS scoping.

Contact for questions:

- Private deployments engineer: lena@redwood.ai
